## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Āsavakkhaya Sutta* ("The Ending of Defilements", Iti 102) is a discourse found in the four-fold division (Catukkanipāta) of the *Itivuttaka*. The text presents a concise exposition on the attainment of liberation, declaring that the destruction of the defilements (*āsavakkhaya*) belongs to one who knows and sees rather than to one who does not. This liberating destruction of suffering is achieved specifically through knowing and seeing the four noble truths: suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the practice leading to its cessation. None of the secondary passages in the reference dossier examine Iti 102 directly; references in the surveyed literature either discuss the doctrinal category of *āsavakkhaya* (the destruction of the taints as the final *abhiññā* or arahantship) or analyze other discourses sharing the same formula.
